key_insight: A founder loss-of-function variant in UBE2L3 was linked to higher sepsis susceptibility in Arab ICU patients, highlighting UBE2L3 as a potential host-directed target for infection biology.
clinical_relevance: The finding may help prioritize genetic risk markers and therapeutic hypotheses for sepsis, but it is not ready for clinical use without replication and functional validation.
method: WGS-based GWAS and exome-wide analysis in 210 Arab ICU patients
REGENIE Firth regression with deleterious-variant prioritization (CADD > 20)
Replication-style support from All of Us burden analysis and AI target scoring
evidence_signal: Among 68 sepsis cases and 142 ICU controls, a novel UBE2L3 start-loss variant appeared in 3 cases and 0 controls (Fisher’s exact P = 0.026), with additional support from an All of Us bacterial-infection burden signal (SKAT-O P = 2.38×10-3).
watch_item: The signal is based on a small founder cohort with rare-variant counts and wide confidence intervals, so effect estimates and target usefulness need independent replication.
paper_title: Genome-Wide Association Study of Sepsis Susceptibility in ICU Patients Identifies Arab Founder Loss-of-Function Variant in UBE2L3
